source_quality_scale.4: official primary HSE regulator guidance; current duty, assessment, control, planning, maintenance or response action verified
source_quality_scale.3: official primary source with a material building, system, space, height, substance, surface, crowd, electrical, emergency or response applicability caveat

quality_guards: Asbestos controls depend on building age, material type, location, condition, accessibility, planned disturbance, occupancy and survey quality.
Legionella controls depend on water-system design, temperature, stagnation, aerosol generation, maintenance, occupancy and monitoring results.
Confined-space controls depend on geometry, atmosphere, process residues, isolations, ingress routes, work activity, entrants and rescue capability.
Work-at-height controls depend on fall distance, edges, openings, fragile surfaces, access, weather, equipment, supervision and rescue planning.
DSEAR controls depend on substance inventory, physical state, concentration, ventilation, containment, ignition sources, process conditions and emergency arrangements.
Slip-and-trip controls depend on flooring, contamination, drainage, housekeeping, footwear, lighting, weather, traffic and maintenance.
Crowd controls depend on attendance, audience profile, venue design, entry and exit capacity, transport, weather, behaviour, staffing and emergency coordination.
Electrical controls depend on voltage, fault energy, system design, earthing, isolation, environment, equipment condition, work method and competence.
Emergency controls depend on site hazards, occupancy, shift patterns, layout, alarm coverage, escape routes, responder access, communications and exercises.
First-aid provision depends on workplace hazards, workforce size and distribution, operating hours, vulnerable people, remoteness and emergency-service access.
Asbestos evidence is building-, material-, condition- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level exposure or disease probability.
Legionella evidence is system-, operation-, time- and population-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Confined-space evidence is space-, task-, atmosphere- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fatality or injury probability.
Work-at-height evidence is task-, location-, equipment- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fall probability.
DSEAR evidence is substance-, process-, inventory- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or explosion probability.
Slip-and-trip evidence is route-, surface-, activity- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Crowd evidence is event-, venue-, audience- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level crushing or injury probability.
Electrical evidence is system-, equipment-, task- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level shock, fire or explosion probability.
Emergency-procedure evidence is incident-, site-, occupancy- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level consequence probability.
First-aid evidence is workplace-, workforce-, hazard- and response-specific and is not an exact parcel-level survival or injury probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
